title: On-premises data gateway June 2026 release
summary: Microsoft's release notes for on-premises data gateway version 3000.322 (June 2026), covering a new Windows Web Account Manager authentication option, an Apache Log4j security update, a consent-driven diagnostics upload capability surfaced in Dataflow Gen2, and alignment with the June 2026 Power BI Desktop release.
audience: Gateway administrators and Fabric/Power BI platform teams responsible for keeping on-premises connectivity current and secure.
why_it_matters: Gateway version compatibility with Power BI Desktop directly affects whether scheduled refreshes execute with the same query engine behavior as the desktop authoring tool, and staying current is also how organizations pick up gateway security patches like the Log4j update.
takeaways: Version 3000.322 adds Windows Web Account Manager (WAM) as an authentication option, intended to strengthen token security and align with Microsoft's modern identity platform.
The bundled Apache Log4j library is updated to 2.25.4 to address previously identified vulnerabilities.
A new consent-driven diagnostics upload capability is introduced, with diagnostic insights surfaced directly in the Dataflow Gen2 run experience.
This gateway version is aligned with the June 2026 release of Power BI Desktop so that gateway-refreshed reports use the same query execution runtime as the desktop authoring tool.
Gateway administrators can trigger gateway updates directly from the Manage connections and gateways experience in Fabric rather than a separate installer step.

claims.text: The June 2026 on-premises data gateway release is version 3000.322, focused on gateway manageability, operational visibility, and enterprise governance while preserving secure connectivity between on-premises sources and Fabric services.
Version 3000.322 adds support for Windows Web Account Manager (WAM) authentication, intended to improve token security and align gateway authentication with Microsoft's modern identity platform.
This release updates the gateway's bundled Apache Log4j library to version 2.25.4 to address previously identified vulnerabilities.

The release introduces a consent-driven model for enabling gateway diagnostic uploads, giving organizations explicit control over how operational diagnostic data is shared, intended to speed up troubleshooting.
Gateway diagnostic information is integrated directly into the Dataflow Gen2 run experience, so administrators and support teams can view relevant diagnostics without switching to a separate tool.

Using the new diagnostic capabilities requires the gateway to be running the latest on-premises data gateway version; Microsoft recommends keeping the gateway updated for security and troubleshooting improvements.
Gateway administrators can initiate gateway updates directly from the Manage connections and gateways experience in Microsoft Fabric, rather than only via a standalone installer.

This gateway version is aligned with the June 2026 release of Power BI Desktop so that reports published and refreshed through the gateway execute queries using the same runtime/logic as that Power BI Desktop version.
